basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 5.' and it opens '(Cap. XXXVIII.—Vers. 5.) Et adjecit, et peperit filium, et vocavit nomen ejus Selom; haec'. Migne prints the chapter at the head of this block.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XXXVIII.—Vers. 5.) Et adjecit, et peperit filium, et vocavit nomen ejus Selom; haec autem erat in Chazbi, quando peperit eum. Verbum Hebraeum hic pro loci vocabulo positum est, quod Aquila pro re transtulit, dicens: Et vocavit nomen ejus Selom. Et factum est ut mentiretur in partu postquam genuit Selom. Postquam enim genuit Selom, stetit partus ejus. Chazbi ergo non nomen loci, sed mendacium dicitur. Unde et in alio loco scriptum est: Mentietur opus olivae, id est, fructum oliva non faciet (Abac. III, 17).
